investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only (INSUFFICIENT — no escalation to Level 2/3/4 was possible or attempted; see notes below). All retained evidence acquired via plain curl (raw HTTP, no WebFetch/AI-markdown conversion, real descriptive User-Agent) plus independent DNS lookups (nslookup) and two independent alternative TLS client implementations (PowerShell/.NET Invoke-WebRequest and the WebFetch tool's own remote OpenSSL-based fetch infrastructure), used only to corroborate a genuine, real transport-layer reachability finding — never to bypass, authenticate past, or otherwise defeat any access control. The prior loose sources/porto.json lead's official_website (https://www.planobporto.com) was found to be DNS NXDOMAIN, corroborated by two independent resolvers (this machine's local nslookup and the WebFetch tool's own separate remote resolver). The only variant that resolves at all, the bare domain https://planobporto.com, resolves to a live IP (50.62.172.212) but fails a TLS handshake to port 443 reproduced across three independent TLS client stacks (curl/Schannel, PowerShell/.NET, WebFetch/OpenSSL) from at least two independent network vantage points. A plain, unencrypted HTTP (port 80) request to the same bare domain reaches a Cloudflare-fronted edge that itself returns HTTP 409 with the literal body 'error code: 1001' — Cloudflare's own documented code for 'DNS resolution error', meaning even Cloudflare's own edge cannot reach whatever origin is configured behind this hostname today. Because no HTTP response body was ever obtained from the candidate's own live site under any protocol/client combination, there was no HTML, JS, or bootstrap data available to inspect, so a genuine, non-fabricated Level 2 (STRUCTURAL) escalation was not possible — there was nothing structural to inspect. To responsibly distinguish 'the venue itself no longer exists' from 'only its website is currently broken' (a DEFER-vs-REJECT question, not fact acquisition), this investigation additionally retained the Wayback Machine's own availability API + CDX snapshot history for this domain (showing the site was genuinely live for many years, publishing real WordPress-shaped /events/ and /event/{slug}/ pages, before beginning to return 404/absent responses from October 2022 onward) and one retained historical snapshot of the site's own former homepage (2022-03-15), plus one retained fetch of a third-party listing (Songkick's own venue page), used explicitly and only as corroborating discovery-lead context per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's 'Third-party sources' section, never as first-party fact authority. A dependency-free, no-network Node offline-proof script re-parsed every retained evidence file to mechanically re-confirm every unreachability/corroboration claim below.

probe_history.reason: Plain, unauthenticated requests to every resolvable form of the candidate's official domain failed to return any usable content. https://www.planobporto.com (the exact official_url recorded in the prior loose sources/porto.json lead) is DNS NXDOMAIN, independently corroborated by two separate resolvers (local nslookup and the WebFetch tool's own remote DNS resolution — see evidence/dns-lookups.txt and evidence/tls-probe-log.txt). The only variant that resolves at all, https://planobporto.com (bare domain, no www), resolves to a real IP (50.62.172.212) but fails the TLS handshake itself on every attempt, reproduced across three independent TLS client implementations (curl/Schannel, PowerShell/.NET, and the WebFetch tool's own separate OpenSSL-based infrastructure) from at least two independent network vantage points — this is not a single client's misconfiguration. A plain HTTP (port 80, unencrypted) request to the same bare domain does reach a live Cloudflare-fronted edge, but that edge itself returns HTTP 409 with body 'error code: 1001' (Cloudflare's own documented 'DNS resolution error' code, meaning Cloudflare's own edge cannot resolve/reach whatever backend origin is configured for this hostname) — reproduced identically for both the homepage and /robots.txt, ruling out a path-specific cause. No HTML, JSON-LD, RSS, ICS, JS bundle, or any other content was obtained from the candidate's own live site under any protocol or client tested. This already conclusively answers the passive-static question (no usable data is currently exposed by this candidate's own official presence, under any client), and there is no HTML/JS/bootstrap data of any kind to inspect for a genuine Level 2 escalation — Level 2 requires actual retained page content to analyse, which does not exist here. Per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's 'DEFER does not require exhausting the ladder', a single retained INSUFFICIENT Level 1 entry is sufficient grounds to reach DEFER without fabricating a Level 2/3/4 attempt that has nothing real to act on.

Per the prior loose sources/porto.json lead ('plano-b-porto') and third-party listings retained by this investigation (Songkick); NOT independently confirmed today via first-party live evidence, because the candidate's own official website is currently unreachable under every protocol/client tested — see identity below.

identity.notes: Identity cannot honestly be marked PROVEN today: the candidate's official website is currently completely unreachable under every protocol/client tested (see probe_history), so no CURRENT first-party evidence of self-identification exists. However, a retained Wayback Machine snapshot of this exact domain's own former homepage (2022-03-15, evidence/body-archive-snapshot.html — a byte-retained copy of what planobporto.com's own server literally served, not an AI summary) self-identifies with <title>PLANO B :: PROGRAMAÇÃO</title> and links its own social accounts (facebook.com/planobclub, instagram.com/planobporto) — genuinely first-party historical identity evidence, just not current. The retained CDX snapshot history (evidence/body-cdx-recent.txt, evidence/body-cdx-historical.txt is actually named body-cdx.txt) further shows this exact domain was live and publishing real, dated events (e.g. 'Aniversário Plano B', touring DJ/live bookings) continuously from at least 2007 through 2021, then began returning 404/absent responses from October 2022 onward — consistent with a real, long-running venue whose website specifically broke at some point, not a domain that was never genuinely this venue's. This investigation additionally retained one third-party page (Songkick's own venue listing, evidence/body-songkick.html) purely as a DISCOVERY LEAD to check whether the real-world venue is still operating at all (relevant to choosing DEFER over REJECT) — never as authority for any first-party fact. That page's own JSON-LD repeats a street address ('Rua Cândido Dos Reis, 30', Porto, 4050-151) matching the prior loose registry lead's physical_address, and lists several dated 2026 concerts at this venue. Per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md, this third-party corroboration is recorded honestly as context, not promoted to identity proof. Net assessment: PARTIAL/MEDIUM — strong historical first-party evidence this domain was genuinely Plano B's own site, plus third-party corroboration the real venue is still operating, but no current first-party confirmation this exact domain is still under the same control today, since it cannot currently be reached at all.

site_classification.platform: Cannot be classified from current live evidence — the site is entirely unreachable today (see probe_history). Historically (per retained Wayback CDX + the 2022-03-15 snapshot only): 2007-2021 CDX entries show WordPress-shaped URL conventions (/events/, /event/{slug}/, /comments/feed/, /author/planob/, akismet-plugin-probe 404s), but the retained 2022-03-15 snapshot itself shows the site had migrated to a bespoke, hand-built static-asset front end (Bootstrap 5.1.3 via jsDelivr CDN, jQuery 3.5.1, a local assets/css/stylesheet.css and assets/js/general.js, Typekit web fonts) with no WordPress generator meta tag or wp-content path visible in that snapshot. This is offered only as historical platform context, not a current classification — a future re-investigation, once/if the domain becomes reachable again, would need to re-establish this from scratch rather than assume either platform still applies.
